FN-ARGIKSQ-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 445
Committee: Health Sponsor: Representative Andy Whitt
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: «Released Date»
House Bill 445 as introduced would increase receipts to the following by an undetermined
amount dependent on the receipts from the 7% excise tax levied on the gross sales of
consumable hemp products to retailers and would require these proceeds to be distributed as
follows:
State General Fund 50%
Counties (on a prorated basis per population) 25%
Municipalities (on a prorated basis per population) 25%
This bill would increase the obligations of the Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Board by an
undetermined amount dependent upon the cost of storage spaces for seized contraband,
additional personnel, and other administrative costs associated with the licensure and regulation
of these products. However, these obligations would be offset, in whole or in part by the
following fees provided by this bill which would be deposited to the Consumable Hemp Product
Compliance Fund, created by this bill, in the State Treasury: (1) the $50 initial license fee for
retailers; (2) the $50 label approval fee for manufacturers; and (3) the annual license fees for
consumable hemp products as follows:
Manufacturer License Fee $5,000
Wholesaler License Fee $5,000
Retailer License Fee $1,000
This bill could also increase receipts to the State General Fund from civil penalties imposed by
the ABC board up to $20,000 per offense; could increase receipts to the State General Fund and
municipal general funds from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general
funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could

funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could
FN-ARGIKSQ-2
increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, and local jails by an
undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the
offenses provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.
This bill would also increase the obligations of the Alabama Department of Public Health by an
undetermined amount to review certificates of analysis submitted to the department for certain
consumable hemp products, which would be offset, in whole or in part, by a processing fee
collected by the department in an amount set by the department.
Lastly, this bill could decrease potential receipts to the State General Fund and municipal
general funds by an amount ranging from $50 to $400 per violation by repealing Section
13A-12-214.4, Code of Alabama 1975, regarding fines for possession of certain cannabinoids.
